subject: Computer Networking
title: ISPs and How You Connect
description: A fast breakdown of ISPs and How You Connect for builders.

hook.text: You pay one company for internet. That company connects you to the rest of the world. That's your ISP.

buildup.text: Tier 3 ISPs serve homes and businesses. Tier 2 ISPs serve regions. Tier 1 ISPs form the global backbone.

discovery.text: Tier 1 providers peer with each other for free. Everyone else pays someone upstream for transit.

twist.text: Your ISP can see which domains you visit. That's why VPNs and encrypted DNS matter for privacy.

climax.text: In some countries, a single ISP controls nearly all access. That gives them enormous power over citizens.

punchline.text: Your ISP is your gateway. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: What is a Tier 1 ISP?
options: A provider that forms part of the internet's global backbone
An ISP that only serves residential customers

details.summary: Internet Service Providers connect your home or business to the internet through technologies like fiber, cable, DSL, or wireless. ISPs operate at different tiers: Tier 1 carriers own backbone networks, Tier 2 regional providers buy transit, and Tier 3 local ISPs sell access to consumers.
details.whyItMatters: ISPs are the gatekeepers of internet access. Their infrastructure and policies directly determine your connection speed, reliability, and cost.
takeaways: ISPs provide the physical connection between you and the internet
Tier 1 carriers own backbone, Tier 2 are regional, Tier 3 are local
Connection technologies include fiber, cable, DSL, and wireless

faq.question: Why do ISP speeds vary so much?
faq.answer: Speed depends on the last-mile technology: fiber offers gigabit speeds, cable shares bandwidth among neighbors, DSL degrades with distance from the exchange. ISPs also oversell bandwidth, assuming not all users will peak simultaneously. Congestion during peak hours reduces actual speeds.

faq.question: What is the difference between ISP tiers?
faq.answer: Tier 1 carriers like AT&T and NTT own global backbone networks and peer with each other without paying. Tier 2 providers have regional networks and pay Tier 1 for global reach. Tier 3 ISPs buy from Tier 2 and sell access to consumers. Your data traverses multiple tiers.
